selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the story, what were the two soldiers told to do at the beginning?
questions.answer: They were ordered to travel to a faraway city.

questions.question: What choice faced both soldiers?
questions.answer: They had to choose between two different roads.

questions.question: What did the guide say about the left side?
questions.answer: He said it gave no benefit and most who took it lost.

questions.question: Which road had rules and authority over it?
questions.answer: The road on the right.

questions.question: What bad things were connected with the left-hand road?
questions.answer: No real gain and loss for most travelers.

questions.question: Which soldier is called fortunate in the story?
questions.answer: The one who chose the right road.

questions.question: What bigger troubles was he saved from inside himself?
questions.answer: He was saved from great fear and from having to depend on other people.

questions.question: What kind of person was the second soldier by the end?
questions.answer: A rebel and deserter who faced punishment.

questions.question: Who met the two soldiers when the road split?
questions.answer: A man standing at the fork spoke to them.

questions.question: What did the man at the fork say about the road on the right?
questions.answer: He said it usually brought benefit and peace of mind, with no real loss.

questions.question: What did he say about the left road’s outcome for most people?
questions.answer: Most people who took it ended up harmed and without gain.

questions.question: What did the successful soldier do after hearing the advice?
questions.answer: He chose the road on the right.

questions.question: What did the right-road travelers have to carry besides food?
questions.answer: A strong rifle.

questions.question: Which soldier is called luckless?
questions.answer: The one who chose the left road.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier who left the army’s way?
questions.answer: He traveled in need, afraid of everything, and begging from people.

questions.question: Why is the obedient soldier described as fearing no one?
questions.answer: Because he was prepared and was walking the proper path.

questions.question: What two things does the passage compare at the start?
questions.answer: It compares worship with profit and happiness, and wrongdoing with loss and ruin.

questions.question: According to him, how often did the right road lead to good results?
questions.answer: Most of the time, with nine out of ten travelers doing well.

questions.question: How were the two roads alike?
questions.answer: They were the same in distance.

questions.question: What hidden advantage did the right road offer?
questions.answer: It gave protection, order, and a good ending.

questions.question: What kind of weight did he carry physically?
questions.answer: He carried a manageable amount of equipment.

questions.question: Even though he carried less on his body, what heavier load did he gain?
questions.answer: He gained deep worry, fear, and dependence on others.

questions.question: What happened when the disobedient soldier finally arrived?
questions.answer: He was punished for rebellion and desertion.

questions.question: What burden did the successful soldier carry on his back?
questions.answer: He carried a moderate load of supplies and equipment.
